correctness.rationale: The Fibonacci companion matrix has exact least period 10*11^(k-1). Nine regular index classes have normalized increment (F_(i+10t)-F_(i+10s))/(11(t-s)) congruent to 8L_i (nonzero modulo 11), proving each isometric. The exceptional class i=5 has a rigorously derived 11-adic identity F_(5+10t)=κ+242V(t)^2 with V(t) an isometry. Each solution to the square congruence mod 11^(k-2) contributes exactly 11 index classes mod 11^(k-1). k=1 is separately counted, zero and nonzero roots are handled. Direct exact-arithmetic complete-period histograms agree at k=1,...,6, independent root-count enumeration at e=1,2,3. Finite tests are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The strongest same-prime and same-sequence sources characterize attained-value images, not their complete index multiplicities; the available general frequency theorem has inapplicable hypotheses. Full published Lucas-seven fiber result and Fibonacci-prime-three distribution are different problems. Exact index preimage law and regular/critical counts were compared by implication, with the inaccessible 1999 general-frequency work retained as a genuine originality risk. Searches are negative evidence, not proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: The 1999 Carlip–Somer regular-frequency chapter could contain a stronger general formula; only bibliographic metadata and its characterization in 2007 were available. An authorized attempted full-text retrieval required human interaction and was not bypassed.
Published Rowland–Yassawi image-level proofs provide useful tools that might yield some components implicitly; no explicit complete per-target index-frequency formula was located.
An unindexed specialized table or equivalent weighted p-adic result could still predate this proof; human priority review is warranted.

value.rationale: The number of occurrences of each output in a least recurrence period is a standard independently meaningful arithmetic invariant. The result resolves every finite precision of the natural p=11 question motivated by earlier work on attainable-value density. It reveals three distinct regular weights and an exceptional quadratic tower with arbitrarily high multiplicity, which the known limiting image density alone cannot recover. Explicit all-k formulas have reusable arithmetic and distributional significance without claiming results at other primes.
